title: Encryption at rest and in transit

videos.script: The data is encrypted. It is the most reassuring sentence in a security review. And on its own it says almost nothing. {{claim}} Encrypted where? With a key held by whom? Against which person? {{questions}} A customer's record crosses a network, lives in a server's memory, sits in data files and travels in a backup. Each place has a different reader, and a different kind of encryption. {{path}} In this lesson the database already speaks TLS, with a certificate nobody can check. The data files hold every e-mail address in clear. A backup copies them out in clear too. {{findings}} One by one, Ana closes each gap. A certificate worth checking. A server that insists on it. A program that logs in with a key instead of a password. A disk that is useless when stolen. {{fixes}} And one attempt that goes wrong in an instructive way. The key ends up in the server's log. {{log}} Every form of encryption ends somewhere. The question to keep asking is who is standing there. {{end}}
